messages:
Emma: Hey team — AcmeCorp EU is ready to start a 30-day POC but their security/Risk says they need: 1) a simple data flow diagram for the POC, 2) confirmation of data residency (no customer data leaves EU), 3) a current subprocessor list and roles, and 4) whether any telemetry/analytics are aggregated outside the region. They want this by EOD Wed. Can we pull the artifacts together?

Alex: Short answer: for Redwood Hosted we have regional processing for inference in eu-west-1 for EU customers by default, but some product telemetry (aggregate metrics/error rates) are anonymized and routed to our central analytics in us-east for product ops. For Dedicated/Private, everything can remain in-customer VPC/region.

Maria: We can provide a signed subprocessor CSV + DPA addendum. Also can add a sentence to confirm we won't export customer content outside EU for the duration of the POC (if Hosted inference pinned to EU region). Need to know if they require any additional contractual language.

Ben: Dataflow sketch below — use this for the diagram:

```
Client -> HTTPS -> Load Balancer (eu-west-1)
  -> Inference Pool (GPUs, eu-west-1)
    -> KV cache / prefix-cache (ephemeral, eu-west-1)
    -> Outputs -> return to client
Logs/metrics: app logs (redacted) -> regional log store (eu-west-1)
Metrics (aggregated counters) -> telemetry aggregator -> optional export to us-east analytics
```

Ben: Implementation notes: Hosted POC in EU will keep request/response payloads in eu-west-1. Control plane metadata (org, billing events) is global but we can suppress any PII. If they require zero outbound telemetry, we can disable the telemetry export for the POC — ops change with config flag.

Oliver: For commercial team — if they want guaranteed residency for the POC, recommend Dedicated reserved pool in eu region. That will increase monthly cost (estimate: +40% on top of hosted usage for reserved capacity) but solves residency + isolation ask. Need to confirm POC throughput to size.

Emma: @Alex @Maria can you confirm the exact phrasing we should put in the diagram & CSV? I want to send a single zip to Acme security with: diagram PNG, subprocessor CSV, short note on telemetry and a one-paragraph residency statement.

Alex: Suggested phrasing for residency note: "During the AcmeCorp POC, inference requests, model KV cache, and application logs will be processed and stored in eu-west-1. Aggregated, non-identifying telemetry may be exported to our central analytics in us-east for product operations unless explicitly disabled for the customer POC." Use that and mark telemetry as toggleable.

Maria: I'll generate the subprocessor CSV and attach the DPA addendum. Items to include: cloud provider (GCP/Region), monitoring vendor (Datadog), CDNs, third-party model providers (if any inference uses external weights), and our logging provider. I'll mark roles: subprocessor, subprocessors locations, and contact.

Ben: Internal doc links (for the diagram & ops playbook): https://intranet.redwood/docs/poc-residency and https://intranet.redwood/ops/telemetry-flags — include in the zip.

ComplianceBot: Automated note: SOC2, ISO27001 controls referenced. Contact compliance@redwood for attestation copies.

Oliver: I'll draft the diagram PNG from Ben's ASCII and prep the pricing delta note. Emma, can you confirm target POC start date?

Emma: Target start is next Monday. I'll aim to send the package to Acme by Friday EOD so they have weekend to review. Assignments: Maria -> subprocessor CSV + DPA, Ben -> PNG diagram + ops note on telemetry toggle, Alex -> residency language + approval, Oliver -> pricing delta. I'll compile and send. Thanks! :thumbsup:
